title.narrative: Strengthening civic peace initiatives of Palestinian youth inspired by integral ecology approach

description.narrative: The impact of the long running occupation, compounded by the COVID-19 pandemic has left deep scars in Palestinian communities on the West Bank. The economy, especially tourism, has been greatly affected. Public life has increasingly become characterized by a lack of law and order, a decline of values, a surge in violence against women, and, given the lack of a viable peace process, a pervading sense of hopelessness and despair, particularly amongst young people. The ongoing Israeli occupation and creeping annexation as a result of the expansion of settlements and the taking over of area C in the West Bank has a great impact on many people’s livelihoods. In this context, developing integrated advocacy capacities among disadvantaged Palestinian groups has become more important. AEI and CAFOD implemented a 3-year EU Peacebuilding Initiative funded project between 2017-2020 focussed on equipping and empowering youth to become leaders in their communities, agents for positive change despite the prevailing political realities and supported them to design and implement advocacy initiatives in their local communities. This project will build on key elements of this including the piloting and strengthening of innovative tools for monitoring impact. The project will explore the concept of ‘encounter’ between Christians and Muslims and between rural and urban Palestinian communities in order to overcome the imposed fragmentation that hinders local level peace. The project will test and develop M&E tools for peacebuilding and will also look at the role of the environment in advocacy messages and how to protect Palestinian land against encroaching Israeli settlements. The project will pilot educational ‘tourism’ led by its youth participants – an innovative approach inspired by the previous EU project.
